title: After Eight Weeks of Overseas Study at the Medical University of Vienna
paragraphs: I took part in an eight-week overseas study program at the Medical University of Vienna in March and April 2023, and was allowed to train for two weeks each in a total of four departments of the university general hospital (hereafter AKH): pediatrics, radiology, obstetrics and gynecology and breast surgery, and anesthesiology. In this report, I would like to write focusing especially on the impressive clerkships in pediatrics and anesthesiology.

In the first two weeks at the AKH, within pediatrics I was allowed to rotate through the NICU in the first week and pediatric cardiology in the second week. Because in the fifth-year pediatrics polyclinic clerkship I had had no chance to meet pediatric cardiology patients, being able to train in the second week on a team with patients who had diseases I had only seen in textbooks was especially educational. Furthermore, in the pediatric cardiology clerkship, the doctor who was the ward leader gave us the assignment of trying, with students only, to physically examine patients and interpret ECGs and report a summary to the supervising doctor, so every day I physically examined several patients with congenital heart disease myself, and, based especially on the auscultation results, discussed the examination findings with the Erasmus student who was rotating with me and explained the patients' pathophysiology including the ECG interpretation, which was good training. The patients' families also cooperated greatly, and by examining almost all the patients at the station every day and new patients, and further comparing findings from patient to patient, I could feel my auscultation and examination skills improve day by day. I was also allowed to take part in the catheter treatments handled by pediatric cardiology, and since I could study not only pediatric cardiology but also anesthesiology, my own field of interest, in terms of how to sedate the patient, it was a very useful opportunity.

Meanwhile, in anesthesiology, which I rotated through in the last two weeks, I was allowed to train for two weeks with the anesthesiology team dedicated to trauma surgery. The trauma surgery station handled not only scheduled trauma operations but also the first touch of trauma patients brought in by ambulance, and as an anesthesiology trainee I was allowed to take part not only in surgical anesthesia but also in the response in the shock room. Furthermore, because it was my own field of interest, I was allowed to join a resident on the night shift of general anesthesiology, and I also had the opportunity to observe widely the anesthesiology department of the University of Vienna, one of the largest in Europe. Based on the knowledge from my anesthesiology clerkship at Nagoya University Hospital before going abroad, I noticed differences between Vienna and Nagoya in anesthetic methods, drugs used and operating department work systems, and being able to discuss those differences with the anesthesiology doctors of the AKH on the basis of papers and the regulations of each country was a very educational opportunity to look back on my anesthesiology clerkship at Nagoya University Hospital and learn its characteristics.

Throughout, including radiology and obstetrics and gynecology, all the doctors taught very enthusiastically, they supported me over the language barrier with patients, and I was also able to deepen mutual learning with the local students, and it was precisely because everyone supported and cooperated with me that it became a very fulfilling eight weeks. I will definitely connect the valuable experience gained in the eight weeks to my future career, not only in my skills and knowledge as an anesthesiologist but also in an international career. I would like to take this opportunity to express my heartfelt thanks to Professor 粕谷 and Dr. 長谷川 of the International Collaboration Office of the Nagoya University School of Medicine, who made efforts for this study abroad, the doctors of the International Exchange Department of the Medical University of Vienna, and all the doctors and students I was allowed to be involved with. Thank you.
